title: Introduction to Observability: Logs, Metrics, and Traces
description: Learn the three pillars of observability and why they are essential for modern cloud applications.

data.text: Observability is the ability to understand what is happening inside your application by looking at its external outputs. Unlike traditional monitoring, which tracks known metrics, observability helps you explore and understand unknown problems in complex systems.

terms.definition: Timestamped text records of discrete events, such as user logged in or payment failed.
Numeric measurements aggregated over time, such as CPU usage, request count, or error rate.
Records of a request journey through multiple services, showing where time is spent and where failures occur.
Data collected from running systems, including logs, metrics, and traces.

data.title: The Three Pillars
data.text: Logs tell you what happened. Metrics tell you how much or how often. Traces tell you where time went. Together, they give you a complete picture of your application health.

data.caption: The three pillars of observability
data.definition:
graph TD
    A[Application] --> L[Logs: Events]
    A --> M[Metrics: Numbers over time]
    A --> T[Traces: Request paths]
    L --> D[Developer / SRE]
    M --> D
    T --> D

data.title: Why Observability Matters
items: Debug production issues without reproducing them locally.
Detect performance bottlenecks before users notice.
Understand the impact of code changes on system behavior.
Meet compliance requirements for audit trails.

data.title: Log vs. Metric vs. Trace (Real Example)
data.code:
LOG:    "Payment service error: connection timeout to gateway"
METRIC: payment_service.http_errors_total{code="500"} = 42 (last 5 min)
TRACE:  checkout-request-789 -> inventory-service [12ms] -> payment-service [timeout]

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Observability helps you understand unknown problems in complex systems.
Logs, metrics, and traces are the three pillars.
Azure provides integrated tools for all three: Log Analytics, Metrics, and Application Insights.
You need all three pillars for full observability.
data.takeaway: Next, you will explore Azure Monitor, the central platform that brings all telemetry together.
